transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Start time: 15:00 UTC 
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Liam (Monolith CISO), Priya (Cloud Architect), Diego (DevOps)

Summary (auto): Quick security review focused on encryption at rest/in-transit and key sourcing options. Customer leaning to BYOK via their on-prem HSM for regulated PII; wants details on HSM connector, envelope encryption, audit logs and RBAC controls. Agreed next steps: share BYOK playbook, schedule HSM POC spike, provide SOC2/FIPS attestation.

Topics: BYOK options, HSM connector (KMIP/PKCS#11), envelope encryption, audit log retention and format, RBAC/SSO integration, data residency mapping, operational playbooks (rotation, escrow).

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, do you all see my screen? 
[00:06] Priya: yep seeing it. thanks, we'll kick off from the compliance side first.
[00:11] Liam: thanks. quick context: we're Monolith, heavy regulated PII workloads, need strong proofs for auditors - SOC 2, and we also have EU data residency requirements. main ask today is how Redwood handles keys and if we can bring our HSM.
[00:23] Maya: great, that's the right framing. we're going to walk through at-rest and in-transit encryption, then BYOK and HSM integration patterns. note: some transcriptions below may mis-say PKCS 11 as PKCS eleven, apologies. 
[00:36] Diego: also we're sensitive to latency for real-time inference path, so wrap/unwrap latency matters; also we have some batch jobs where cost is more important.

[02:05] Jordan: first, at-rest - Redwood encrypts model weights and token cache using AES-256-GCM, keys are stored in our KMS for hosted mode. for private/dedicated we offer two options: our managed KMS with envelope encryption, or BYOK where you supply a key from your HSM.
[02:29] Priya: when you say envelope, what's the key hierarchy look like? are you using a per-tenant data key or a single key for multiple tenants?
[02:37] Maya: good question. we create per-tenant data keys derived from a root key — the customer root if BYOK — and we rotate at the data-key layer periodically. envelope keys wrap the data-keys, so your HSM only needs to perform wrap/unwrap.
[02:51] Liam: and the HSM integration, do you support KMIP or PKCS#11? we are an nCipher/Thales shop and we prefer KMIP.
[03:00] Maya: we support both KMIP and PKCS#11 for the HSM adapter; we also have a Cloud HSM connector for AWS/Azure/GCP HSMs. for KMIP we can run an adapter in your VPC that proxies requests to your on-prem HSM.
[03:18] Priya: what about attestation and certifications? auditors ask for FIPS / tamper evidence and attestations from vendors.
[03:24] Jordan: Redwood can share our FIPS-validated module list and FIPS attestation, plus we can provide our SOC 2 Type II report. for customer HSMs, we rely on the vendor's FIPS 140-2/3 attestation — that's what auditors expect.

[05:12] Diego: latency again — if every inference needs a wrap/unwrap call to HSM, that's going to add overhead. what's the recommended pattern?
[05:21] Maya: recommended is envelope encryption with asymmetric wrapping for the long-term key and caching of unwrapped data keys in the serving runtime's secure KV cache. we call that the KV cache but I've seen transcripts call it KV "cash" so, the idea is the runtime caches decrypted data-keys for active sessions to avoid hitting HSM for every token.
[05:44] Diego: okay, how do you ensure cache isn't comprom — like if a node is reprovisioned?
[05:49] Maya: the cache is ephemeral and tied to the instance; keys are zeroed on termination. also we persist only wrapped keys in storage. we support rotation and remote revocation — an admin can revoke a root key and the runtime will fail-safe to a fallback model variant.

[07:10] Priya: about audit logs: we need cryptographic proof of key usage for at least 7 years in our sector. does Redwood provide detailed key usage logs (wrap/unwrap events, user, service principal, IP, etc.)? and can logs be exported to our SIEM?
[07:28] Jordan: yes — we log wrap/unwrap events, requester identity, region, and request metadata. logs can be shipped to your Splunk/Datadog or stored in your object store. retention is configurable; default is 90 days but we offer extended retention as an add-on.
[07:46] Liam: are those logs tamper-evident? we need non-repudiation for audits.
[07:52] Maya: logs are append-only with HMAC chaining internally; for higher assurance we can stream logs to your own write-once storage or to an external SIEM with immutable retention. we'll include the log schema in the playbook.

[09:05] Diego: what about SSO and RBAC for key operations? we want separation of duties — devs shouldn't be able to rotate or export keys.
[09:12] Maya: we integrate with SAML/SSO providers for identity; we also support SCIM provisioning. RBAC is role-based: admin, operator, auditor, read-only. key ops (unwrap/wrap) can be restricted by role and by token-level scope. we can map your AD groups to Redwood roles.
[09:36] Priya: can we require mTLS between our HSM adapter and Redwood runtime? network-level mutual auth?
[09:41] Jordan: yes, POC typically uses mTLS + private peering or VPC endpoints; for private deployments we run the adapter in the customer's VPC to minimize cross-network egress.

[11:05] Liam: walk me through an incident scenario: if a key is suspected compromised, what's the runbook?
[11:12] Maya: step one is immediate rotate the root/wrapping key; then we rewrap all data-keys with the new root. runtime will refuse old-wrapped keys after revocation. we also isolate the impacted nodes, rotate HSM credentials, and provide an evidence package including audit logs and key operation timestamps.
[11:32] Diego: rewrap operation looks expensive. can you do gradual rewraps or is it atomic?
[11:37] Maya: we support background rewrap — you can schedule rolling rewraps by dataset/tenant. you can also use fallback model variants while rewraps run.

[13:10] Priya: for BYOK the onboarding steps we expect: connector deployment in our VPC, key import/export policy, test wrap/unwrap, and performance bench. what's Redwood's typical timeline?
[13:20] Jordan: usually 2–4 weeks for the initial POC spike: 1 week to provision connector and smoke test, 1–2 weeks for bench and integration, and then formal sign-off and pilot. depends on customer's change windows.
[13:35] Liam: any blockers for us? we have an internal escrow policy — keys must be able to be exported to a vault for legal hold. do you support key escrow?
[13:42] Maya: we don't hold customer private keys by default; escrow is possible via an approved vault process or a third-party escrow. we can support key import/export flows with strict audit trails but the HSM vendor policy often controls whether raw key material can be exported.

[15:00] Diego: question on envelope algorithm: are you using symmetric data keys with AES-256-GCM and RSA/OAEP for wrapping or do you prefer AES-KW?
[15:09] Maya: AES-256-GCM for data encryption; for key wrapping we support AES-KW (RFC 3394) and RSA-OAEP for asymmetric wraps. also we support ECIES where the HSM vendor prefers EC-based wrapping.

[17:02] Priya: data residency: we need all EU keys to be provisioned inside EU HSMs and logs stored in EU. how do we ensure routing and that no key material leaves the region?
[17:11] Jordan: Redwood can pin keys to regions and use region-aware routing. for private mode we'll deploy connectors and runtime in your EU region; wrapped keys never cross region boundary. we can provide network diagrams in the playbook.
[17:29] Liam: do you have examples of legal language or contract clauses around key custody? auditor wants explicit clause that Redwood cannot access customer unwrapped keys in BYOK mode.
[17:36] Jordan: yes, we have contract language and we can provide an addendum that specifies no access to raw key material and describes data handling obligations. will attach to the ticket.

[19:00] Diego: question: for performance bench, what metrics should we measure?
[19:06] Maya: measure wrap/unwrap latency at cold start and steady-state, throughput (wrap ops/sec), separation penalty for mTLS and network hops, memory footprint of caching decrypted data-keys, and end-to-end inference latency with and without cache hits.

[20:40] Priya: about PKI and cert rotation for mTLS — do you support automated cert rotation for connectors?
[20:46] Jordan: yes, cert rotation is automated via our control plane for Redwood-managed connectors; for customer-managed connectors we support short-lived cert issuance via ACME or a manual rotation API.

[22:10] Liam: auditors will also ask for segregation: who can trigger key rotation? can we require dual-approval?
[22:18] Maya: we support multi-person approvers for critical actions; we can require a second approver for root rotation via our console or API. it's a config toggle for high assurance customers.

[24:00] Diego: are we able to integrate with our hardware attestation service to verify HSM firmware and version?
[24:06] Maya: we can accept attestations and record them in the audit trail. for some HSM vendors there's remote attestation APIs — we can capture snapshot reports and attach them to the evidence bundle.

[26:30] Priya: question on backups: if we need disaster recovery of keys, can we back up wrapped keys to our vault and restore them in a different region?
[26:40] Maya: yes you can back up wrapped keys; to restore in a different region you'd need the wrapping key available or import the root into an HSM in target region — which often requires escrow or rekeying. we'll document recommended DR patterns in the playbook.

[28:55] Jordan: quick note on telemetry — we expose token-level cost, latency dashboards, and key op counts in Redwood Console. for security we provide a separate audit dashboard with key event filters.

[30:10] Priya: final question: can we run an isolated on-prem private deployment (airgap) for the most sensitive workload?
[30:18] Maya: yes — private on-prem package is available. in air-gapped mode we'd ship an appliance/container image and a control-plane agent that you run; you manage keys entirely. onboarding time is longer and requires coordination.

[31:50] Liam: ok, this is good. let's recap next steps: BYOK playbook, POC spike for HSM connector, bench test plan, SOC2/FIPS docs.
[32:01] Jordan: yep, we'll share docs and proposed dates. Maya will lead the bench plan. Priya and Diego will prepare infra inventory.

[33:20] Diego: small nit — what about key rotation frequency default?
[33:24] Maya: default data-key rotation is 90 days, root wrap key rotation is annually or on-demand. but we can set to 30 days or shorter if your policy requires it.

[35:00] Priya: auditor often wants proof of key destruction — if we decommission an HSM can we provide attestation that keys were zeroed?
[35:08] Maya: yes — HSM vendors usually provide key destruction certificates; we'll include a process for capturing and storing that artifact.

[37:10] Liam: any gotchas around tokenization or PII scrub before logging? we cannot log raw PII even in traces.
[37:18] Jordan: we recommend deterministic tokenization and PII masking in logs. our default is to redact PII in telemetry; you can opt for additional scrubbing rules at ingestion.

[39:50] Priya: last integration detail — does Redwood support KMIP over TLS with client certs?
[39:56] Maya: yes, KMIP over TLS with client cert auth is supported; we can map client cert CN to a Redwood service principal and audit it.

[41:20] Diego: any large customers using similar patterns we can reference?
[41:25] Jordan: we have references in financial and healthcare sectors; we'll share anonymized case studies and a short reference list.

[43:00] Maya: ok we'll package everything: BYOK playbook, HSM adapter config examples for KMIP/PKCS11, bench plan template, SOC2/FIPS certs, and sample contract language.

[44:30] Liam: sounds good. we'll look to run the POC next week. thanks everyone.
[44:38] Jordan: thanks, talk soon.
